\begin{example} \end{example}[jump in maximal interval]

Source: petersen:page-0191 ↗ def:pet-ch5-geodesically-complete

1. ch5:5.2.7In the punctured plane $\mathbb R^2-\{ (0,0)\} $ the unit-speed geodesic from $(-1,0)$ with tangent $(1,0)$ is defined only on $(-\infty ,1)$, but nearby geodesics from $(-1,0)$ with tangent $(1+\varepsilon _1,\varepsilon _2)$, $\varepsilon _2\ne 0$ small, are defined on all of $\mathbb R$: maximal intervals can jump up in size but, by section 2, not down. \end{example}
